content: Have you noticed that your friend's home looks different from yours at dinner time? Some of your friends live with their grandparents, aunts, and uncles, while some just live with their parents. Why aren't all families exactly the same?
What do you think makes a family? Do you need a lot of people to be a family, or can just two people be a family? Imagine a bird building a nest for just one baby bird. Is that a family?

content.title: Shapes of Families
content.description: Just like shapes are different, families can be big, small, or medium. But they are all beautiful!

content: A family is a group of people who care for and support each other. Families come in different types! Some families are small, where parents and children live together. Some are large, where grandparents, uncles, and cousins live together. And some have just one parent taking care of the children.
Remember, no one type of family is 'better' than another. What makes a family special is the love and care they share for one another!

question: If Rohan lives with his mother, father, grandfather, grandmother, and uncle, what kind of family does he have?

content: Reflection Time: Think about your own family. Who are the people you live with? How do you help each other when someone is sick or feeling sad? Try explaining it in your own words.

Families are like different kinds of trees in a forest. Some trees have many branches, while some are smaller but just as strong. In the animal kingdom too, elephants live in big groups (like a joint family!) while some birds live in small families. The common thing is they all protect each other!
Some students think a family only means people who live in the same house. But sometimes, family members live far away in different cities or even different countries, and they are still your family!
Mastery Challenge: Draw a picture of your family tree! Include everyone you love, and don't forget your pets if you have them! Share it with a friend and ask about their family.
